seo_description: Free, open-source clipboard history for macOS that skips passwords and keys, expires old items, and keeps history AES-encrypted on your Mac. No account.
hero_sub: PrivateClipVault lives in your menu bar and remembers what you copy, minus passwords, card numbers and API keys. History expires on its own and is encrypted on your Mac.
features_sub: Everything stays on your Mac, with no server, no account and no network code.

features.title: Secret detection built in
features.desc: Skips items flagged concealed by password managers, Luhn-valid card numbers, known key prefixes like ghp_ and AKIA, and long high-entropy tokens.

features.title: Items expire automatically
features.desc: Choose a lifetime of 1 minute, 5 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or never. Expired items are removed from disk on the next write.

features.title: Encrypted at rest
features.desc: History is sealed with AES-GCM. The 256-bit key lives in your login keychain, not next to the data.

features.title: Optional Touch ID lock
features.desc: Require Touch ID or your account password to view history. It re-locks after 60 seconds of inactivity and when the screen locks.

features.title: Searchable, click to copy
features.desc: The menu shows your 10 most recent clips. Show All opens a searchable list, and clicking an entry copies it back.

features.title: Control over what is captured
features.desc: Ignore specific apps, pause capture, clear everything, and set history size from 10 to 500 entries. Launch at login is optional.

permissions_step: No special permissions are required; macOS may ask you to approve Login Items in System Settings > General only if you enable Launch at login.

faq.q: Is PrivateClipVault really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, and the full source is on GitHub. There are no ads, accounts, analytics or paid tiers.
None of the privacy permissions: no Accessibility, Screen Recording or Microphone access. It uses the keychain for its own encryption key, and Touch ID only if you turn on the lock.
In an encrypted file at ~/Library/Application Support/PrivateClipVault/vault.sealed on your Mac. The key is in your login keychain, and nothing is ever sent over the network.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, which this free project does not have. Right-click the app and choose Open once to approve it, or build it yourself from source.
